processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Aging at 600 °C for 3 h; incoherent κ particles form within the austenite matrix after higher aging temperature and longer time.

structures.overall_structure: austenite matrix with incoherent κ particles

defect_interactions.interaction_type: incoherent κ particles inhibit crack nucleation during wear test
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: The incoherent κ particles within the austenite matrix, after higher aging temperature and longer time, inhibited crack nucleation during the wear test.

interfaces.phase_evolution: Incoherent κ particles form within the austenite matrix after higher aging temperature and longer time.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: observation of worn surface and wear debris
characterization_methods.purpose: observe the worn surface and wear debris of the 600 °C aged steel
characterization_methods.key_findings: Worn surface shows craters; wear debris consist of irregular flaky fragments; the observation supports that the 600 °C aged steel has good wear resistance.

unmapped_findings: Wear-rate vs aging-time data for Fe–22.33Mn–1.35C–9.87Al (wt%) steel (Figure 8a): for 600 °C aging the linear fit is y = −0.0374x + 0.2146 (R² = 0.99), where y = wear rate ×10³ (mm³/Nm) and x = aging time (h); the 600 °C line lies lowest among the 500 °C (y = −0.0426x + 0.332, R² = 0.97) and 550 °C (y = −0.0399x + 0.2804, R² = 0.93) series. [figure_008]
The 600 °C for 3 h aged steel corresponds to the 3 h endpoint of the 600 °C series in Figure 8a, and is described as having good wear resistance. [b0080, b0081]
SEM of the worn surface of the 600 °C for 3 h aged steel shows craters (100 µm scale bar; 10 µm inset). [figure_008, b0081]
SEM of the wear debris of the 600 °C for 3 h aged steel shows irregular flaky fragments (100 µm scale bar; 10 µm inset of a single plate). [figure_008, b0081]
